headline: The lower easy-run HR now holds across a full block of comparable efforts, no longer a single reading.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The aerobic efficiency shift you've been showing is no longer a one-off — it's now consistent across a full block of comparable-effort runs, with easy paces sitting at a meaningfully lower heart rate than the prior period. That's the kind of within-athlete signal that matters more than any single session, and it's held while your running frequency and pacing stayed in your normal range. This is the confirmation of a genuine adaptation, not variance.

The slight dip in four-week volume is well within consolidation territory and shouldn't be read as anything else — your strength work has actually doubled over the same window, so the total system load is broadly maintained rather than reduced. The picture is one of an athlete redistributing effort across modalities, not backing off.

What's still absent, with the St. Olavsleden crossing approaching, is loaded back-to-back durability — the one demand closest to what that route will ask of you. Nothing in today's data speaks to it either way, so it remains the open question rather than a concern.
watch_items: Whether loaded or consecutive-day efforts start appearing, since pack-carrying durability is the least-tested quality relative to the coming route demands.
Whether the lower easy-run HR continues to translate into faster paces at the same effort, or plateaus once the adaptation settles.
Whether strength volume holds at its raised level or was a temporary spike during the lighter running block.

evidence_items.text: ▼ Easy-run HR averaging 142 bpm vs 155 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 7 runs)
▼ 4-week volume 125 km vs 133 km prior block (-6%)
▲ Zone 2: 191 min vs 180-240 min/week target (106% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 2.8%
